key_insight: Disagreement between fixed numerical rewards and expert judgment can reveal promising materials that automated scores overlook.
engineering_relevance: Expert-informed guidance could broaden generative materials searches beyond rigid objectives, including electronic flatness, synthesizability, and phonon properties.
method: Compare expert judgments of electronic flat bands with a numerical bandwidth score.
Learn expert preferences from pairwise comparisons.
Use learned preferences to guide a crystal diffusion model.
evidence_signal: Expert–score disagreements were systematic beyond an estimated 5% mistaken-label rate, and learned preferences favored reported partially flat-band compounds KCo2As2 and CoGa that the numerical score would discard.
watch_item: Expert preference alignment does not establish experimental performance or synthesis feasibility for generated candidates.
paper_title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
